desc:
You have an array nums of non-negative integers and a list of queries. Query [left, right, cap], when used, lets you lower each element at positions left..right by any amount from 0 to cap, chosen independently for every element.

Queries are used in the given order. Return the smallest k such that after the first k queries the array can be turned into all zeros (exactly zero, never negative). Return 0 if nums is already all zeros, and -1 if even all queries are not enough.

nums = [2, 0, 2], queries = [[0, 2, 1], [0, 2, 1], [1, 1, 3]]
result = 2

After one query every position can lose at most 1, but position 0 holds 2. After two queries every position can lose up to 2, which is enough.
hints: Positions are independent: position i can reach zero after the first k queries exactly when the sum of the caps of the queries (among the first k) that cover it is at least nums[i].
If it works for k queries it also works for k + 1, so the answer can be found by binary search on k.
To test one value of k, build a difference array with +cap at left and -cap at right + 1 for the first k queries, prefix-sum it, and check total[i] ≥ nums[i] for every i.
editorial: Each query offers a 'budget' of at most cap to every position in its range, and a position needs the budget to add up to at least its value (any smaller amount can be used by choosing fewer decrements). So feasibility for a fixed prefix of queries is a pure coverage-sum check, done in O(n + k) with a difference array.
Adding more queries never hurts, so feasibility is monotone in k, which allows binary search over 0..q. If even k = q fails, return -1. Total time O((n + q) log q), space O(n).
